reviews.title: Fix this bug!
reviews.text:
I love what Suno allows me to do creatively, but the lack of proper landscape mode on iPad is a serious accessibility issue. I use an iPad mini 6th generation in a horizontal position because of my physical disabilities caused by a severe brain injury and strokes. The app displays sideways instead of properly adjusting to my screen orientation. I have managed to use it this way since I started using Suno, but it makes the experience unnecessarily difficult.

I write my own lyrics and creative concepts, and Suno helps me bring my music to life when I cannot record my own voice in a traditional studio. This platform means a lot to me, and I want to keep using it. I contacted support and submitted feedback, but I hope the development team takes this accessibility concern seriously and adds proper landscape support for iPad users. Accessibility should help people with disabilities create independently, not make it harder.

reviews.title: Amazing AI music, disastrous customer support
reviews.text:
I genuinely love Suno's music creation capabilities, but its account management and customer support are an absolute disaster.

I contacted support BEFORE changing my phone number in March, specifically to avoid losing access. Seven months later, I'm stuck in a Kafkaesque nightmare: my paid annual Pro subscription is tied to my old phone number, I can't sign in on my new devices, and the only place I can still access my music is an old computer.

Support told me to create a new account and request a transfer of my songs, playlists and personas. I did exactly that. Then they stopped responding. My annual subscription runs until May, leaving me paying for a service I effectively cannot use on my everyday devices.

It's astonishing that a technology company in 2026 cannot change a phone number or migrate a paying customer's account. Suno, please escalate this, restore my access, transfer my music and compensate me for the months of disruption. Great AI music technology deserves far better customer support.

reviews.title: Great at first, frustrating once you want your own sound
reviews.text:
At first, I really liked Suno. It was exciting and easy to turn my own lyrics and ideas into actual songs, and for experimenting with different styles it worked very well.

The problems started when I wanted to move away from the recognizable “Suno sound” and create something that actually sounded like me, with my own style and my own voice.

I have spent a lot of time writing detailed prompts, giving clear production instructions and working with my own voice recordings. Even then, Suno often changes the sound completely, adds an AI-like voice instead of keeping mine natural, ignores instructions, or falls back into the same kinds of intros, instrumental sections and arrangements I specifically asked it not to use.

Editing is also frustrating. Sometimes you only want to fix one small part, but the result changes much more than that.

The biggest issue for me is the credit system. Since September 14, I have used around 9,000 credits, and a significant amount of those have been spent on generations that were unusable through no fault of my own. Songs have been cut off, restarted in the middle, ended incorrectly, repeated sections, changed the arrangement, added unwanted AI vocals or simply ignored the instructions.

Yet the credits are still deducted.

When every failed generation costs credits, trying to refine a song or develop your own sound becomes very expensive very quickly. You can spend hundreds of credits just trying to correct problems created by the generation itse

reviews.title: Suno app
reviews.text:
I personally don’t like the new design of the Suno app. The previous version was much better organized, simpler, and much easier to use when creating songs.

Since the new update, creating songs has become frustrating. I give Suno my own song and expect it to follow what I provided, but instead it often creates something completely different. I try again and again, wasting credits without getting the result I asked for.

As someone who uses Suno seriously for music production, this has made the experience much worse for me. I preferred the old layout and workflow because it was faster, clearer, and more reliable.

Unfortunately, because I kept losing credits without getting the results I wanted, I decided to cancel my subscription.

I really hope Suno listens to its long-time users and brings back the simplicity and reliability of the previous version.

reviews.title: v6 garbage
reviews.text:
After the switch to v6, Suno turned into garbage for me.
Version 5 gave me living solo guitar pieces: nylon, fingers, a melody you could sit down and play on stage. Version 6 spits out bland soundtrack music. The guitar sounds like a cheap synth. Bandoneon, strings and drums crawl in on their own — even when the prompt is one guitarist on a recital stage.
Old prompts that worked for years mean nothing now. Exclude does not work: ban an instrument and that is the instrument you get. A long prompt gets cut down to generic pop-cinema. A short one sometimes saves the tone, but the music is still flat.
They pulled the old models in a single day. There is no way back. Cover and Extend already run on v6, so even a good track from v5 gets ruined if you touch it.
Maybe it works for vocal pop. For concert classical guitar it is a step backwards. Waste of credits, and a waste of what we had.

reviews.title: Great Tech but COMPLETELY Hostile to real musicians/composers
reviews.text:
If you are a serious composer or songwriter looking to use this platform as a tool to add vocals to your own original music, be warned: their system is fundamentally flawed for real creators.
I use this software to add singers to full musical tracks that I entirely composed and wrote myself years ago. Recently, their automated system flagged one of my original tracks, claiming it already matched something in their database. When I reached out to support, they explicitly admitted that their automated copyright detector frequently catches a creator's own original, released work because the system cannot verify who actually owns the uploaded material.
Worse yet, support confirmed they have absolutely no manual override system to clear false flags on a per-track basis. Their official solution to a paying subscriber was to just "work with other music" while they try to build an artist verification system down the road.
The underlying AI vocal generation technology is impressive and works well if operated by the right people, but the lack of basic infrastructure and manual safeguards makes it an incredibly frustrating roadblock for independent artists who own their intellectual property. I have cancelled my subscription and will not return until they implement proper fail-safes and manual human verification for original creators.

reviews.title: Suno — be careful before paying.
reviews.text:
Be very careful before paying for this service.

I paid for a Suno Pro subscription on April 4 and never received access to any Pro features at all. The service has been completely unusable from the moment of purchase.

Support confirmed that the issue is on their side (subscription not linked to my account), but more than two weeks have passed and nothing has been resolved.

This is not just an inconvenience — if you rely on this platform for work, you risk losing time, missing deadlines, and losing money. I personally lost time waiting for a service I paid for instead of moving to an alternative.

At this point, you should be aware that you may pay and receive nothing while the issue remains unresolved.

Proceed with caution.

reviews.title: Suno is a legal thief, be careful.
reviews.text:
If you give your own original compositions to Suno for backing tracks, they acquire all your rights just as you have them, and once you submit your composition, you can't take it back. In other words, they can present your composition to someone else as if they created it, and you cannot claim any rights. They claim they use this to improve their own AI; this is, of course, both true and a clever move. They can use your composition anywhere, sell it to another company, and make money from it without giving you a dime.
I found this out by chance; otherwise, all my compositions would have ceased to be mine. It’s a cleverly designed and prepared system of theft. Moreover, they’ve set everything up on a legal basis. As for the state, it does nothing and will do nothing. Because everyone is looking at the money they’ll make. No one thinks about you. Be smart, do not give away your compositions. Even if you have previously secured all the rights to your composition, be aware that you are now transferring those same rights to them as well.

reviews.title: Amazing music, Terrible experience
reviews.text:
Suno AI offers downright fantastic AI music that still enthralls me thousands of songs later. Although a style can become noticeable it’s not short on the different genres, voices or beats that it can use. The interface is friendly and I mainly used Chat GPT to great effect for making the prompts and lyrics. 

Then why 2 stars? When I logged into my account for the first time on my phone (using my phone number) it logged me into a completely separate new account unaffiliated with my normal one. This account effectively replaced my original one in which I had playlists of songs and an ongoing subscription. This meant that I couldn’t cancel my subscription either. I emailed customer support 4 times on 2 separate addresses with no response (only an ai auto reply). My account still isn’t fixed and I had to manually block Suno from making further transactions from my bank account and subsequently blocked their email from spamming my inbox of failed invoices. I hope this will help you understand my frustration and the fragility of this (very close to being direct fraud).

reviews.title: When It Worked, It Was Great!
reviews.text:
If this app still did what it started out doing, it would have been given a Five star review.  Unfortunately, it didn't, so it wasn't.
Of course, I fully understand that what follows, will not be an issue to most everyone who will make use of this truly amazing system/service.  But, unfortunately however, it's a game stopper for some of us.
Here's the problem, as I see it.  For those of us who are blind, or have severely limited sight, and have need to rely on Apple's VoiceOver text to speech screen reader, there was reasonable access to most of the buttons and features of the app, until around Thanksgiving time in 2025, when we received an app update and all that came to an abrupt halt.  I would have liked to have given Suno a call to discuss the problem, but they don't have a support number.  So, I  sent a few detailed emails describing the problem.  Their support team assured me that accessibility was a priority with Suno.
Well, as I said, "that was before Thanksgiving."  Now it is February, and at least four updates later, and we still don't have access to the service which we are paying for.  Hey, if I can't use it, I cant choose it.

reviews.title: “Incredible Music Ruined by V5 Clipping and Distortion”
reviews.text:
Suno is capable of making genuinely amazing music. The ideas, arrangements, emotion, and compositions it produces are incredible. That’s what makes this so painful.

Version 5 is fundamentally broken when it comes to audio quality.

Inside the app, tracks often sound fine. But the moment you export WAV files, the truth comes out: severe distortion. Every bass hit. Every moment of intensity. Any section with real energy is crushed, clipped, and audibly distorted. This isn’t subtle. It’s not “warm saturation.” It’s hard digital clipping.

I spent over a week trying to save my work—remastering in 4.5, EQing, compressing, limiting, doing everything possible. But the damage is already baked in. When 4.5 reads those clipped sections, you can literally hear the audio drop and collapse because there’s nothing left to recover.

That’s the part that hurts the most. I made some of the best music I’ve ever created here—and it’s effectively unusable.

It feels like Suno’s developers believe that max volume equals quality. It doesn’t.

Louder is not better. Clarity is better.
I can turn up my headphones. I cannot remove distortion that’s already printed into the file.

Suno: hear this clearly.
Drop your output levels in V5. Preserve headroom. Stop brickwalling the mix.
You’re sitting on something incredible—but right now, the audio engine is destroying your own work.

I’ve contacted support. I genuinely hope this is addressed, because Suno could be industry-changing if it stopped confusing

reviews.text:
Asuno is an absolute disaster. I’ve spent a huge amount of credit for nothing, because it simply doesn’t do what you ask. I’m honestly exhausted. The app is good if you just want a random song or something generic, but it never gives you what you really want. It gives you what it wants, and you’re forced to accept it. If you need something specific, forget it. This tool only works for people who are happy with the very first result they get.

To build one single song, I had to request more than 300 covers and remixes of the same track just to find something that barely fit. I spent almost two weeks trying to get the sound I needed to continue my production. That’s ridiculous. The whole experience is horrible because you end up spending money on something you believe will help you, but the actual functionality is not effective at all.

Asuno has potential, but right now it creates more problems than solutions. Users deserve something reliable, not a system that drains credits without delivering what you ask for.
